name: Fisser Sonnenterrasse
kurzbeschreibung: The Fiss Sun Terrace at 1,436 metres in the Upper Inn Valley is Tirol's sunniest high plateau, boasting 2,000 sunshine hours, panoramic vistas, and family alpine parks.
beschreibung:
Überblick

The Fiss Sun Terrace (Fisser Sonnenterrasse) crowns a vast, south-facing mountain plateau at an elevation of 1,436 metres, hovering roughly 500 metres above the Upper Tyrolean Inn Valley. In tandem with its sister villages Serfaus and Ladis, Fiss forms an internationally acclaimed alpine destination blessed by extraordinary climatic fortune: with over 2,000 annual hours of sunshine, this high plateau ranks as one of the sunniest geographic locations in the entire Alps. Framed by the rugged peaks of the Samnaun mountain group to the west and the glaciated Ötztal Alps to the east, guests enjoy an awe-inspiring panorama stretching across the valley basin toward the Swiss border. The 600-year-old village core of Fiss fascinates with clustered Rhaeto-Romanic architecture, historic frescoed gables, and wooden barn lofts. During summer, the sun-drenched plateau serves as the launchpad for innovative adventure parks like the Summer Funpark Fiss at the Möseralm plateau.

Route & Anforderungen

Exploring the Fiss plateau is an accessible delight for visitors of all ages. From the pedestrian-friendly village center, level and barrier-free walking promenades branch outward, while state-of-the-art gondolas (Schönjochbahn and Möseralmbahn) transport adventurers higher into alpine playgrounds. A rich variety of themed walking routes, such as the 'Fisser Gonde' nature trail or the family 'Witches' Trail', can be walked leisurely in one to three hours. Pathways around the village and atop the Möseralm are universally stroller-friendly and dotted with ergonomic sun-loungers. Comfortable walking shoes suffice for the town and sun terraces, whereas sturdy ankle-high hiking boots with lugged rubber soles are recommended for conquering summits around Schönjoch (2,436 metres).

Besuch & Anreise

Travel by car follows motorway A12 or expressway S16 to Landeck, continuing along highway B180 (Reschenstraße) to Ried im Oberinntal, where provincial road L19 ascends the mountainside to Fiss. Large designated car parks are provided at the village edge and gondola terminals. Rail travelers arrive at Landeck-Zams station and board synchronized regional VVT bus services running directly up to Fiss.

Tipps

Head to the 'Kanzel' scenic observation platform at the village periphery in late afternoon: as sunset approaches, the glacial peaks of the Ötztal Alps glow in radiant crimson while the deep Inn Valley below sinks into tranquil twilight. For families, riding the 'Fisser Flitzer' alpine coaster at Möseralm is an unforgettable highlight.
preis: Village grounds and walking paths freely accessible; cable cars and fun rides apply fees
oeffnungszeiten: Plateau accessible year-round; summer cable cars operate mid-June to mid-October
